rows.title_full: THE MAGNA CARTA FOR SENIOR CITIZENS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to integrate into a national comprehensive plan socio-economic and political rights of older persons. It also aims to create a "National Council for the Welfare of Senior Citizens (NCWSC)." This Council shall act as a central authority that would direct, coordinate and integrate the planning, management and implementation of all activities, national and local, public and private, pertaining to the welfare and rights of the elderly, in a manner which will ensure maximum and efficient utilization of human and natural resources.

rows.author: C093
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE ALLOWABLE PERSONAL AND ADDITIONAL EXEMPTIONS OF INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 35 (A) AND 35 (B) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: Section 35(a) and 35(b) of Republic Act 8424 or the Tax Reform Act of 1997 is hereby amended to read as follows: "Section 35. Allowance of Personal Exemption for Individual Taxpayers. (a) In general - For purposes of determining the tax provided inSection 24(a) of this Title, there shall be allowed a basic personal exemption as follows:  'for single individuals or married [P20,000.00] P48,000.00 individuals judicially decreed as legally separated with no dependents'; 'for head of family' [P25,000.00] P54,000.00; 'for each married individual' [P32,000.00] P64,000.00. In the case of married individuals where only one of the spouses is deriving gross income, only such spouse shall be allowed the personal exemption. (b) Additional Exemption ffor Dependents - There shall be allowed an additional exemption of [Eight Thousand Pesos (P8,000.00)] Sixteen Thousand Pesos (P16,000.00) for each dependent not exceeding four(4).  The additional exemption for dependents shall be claimed by only one
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-13

rows.author: C093
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING THE INCOME TAX RATES OF INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CHAPTER III, SECTION 24 (A)(1)(c) OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: What this proposal intends to do is to jumpstart demand in the economy by empowering the consumer with more purchasing power.  This can be done by increasing their take home pay through lower tax rates and hence, lower deductions from their income.  A demand-led growth in these crucial times is indeed the way to go.  There would be a multiplier effect on overall economic growth because this proposal affects virtually all persons earning income.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-13

rows.abstract: All Filipinos abroad, not otherwise disqualified by law who are at least eighteen (18) years of age regardless of their location, work category and residency status abroad, may register as a voter. Any person, who on the day of registration may nothave reached the required age but who, on the day of election shall possess such qualification, may register as a voter.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03570

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING PENALTIES ON PHILIPPINE CONSULATE OFFICIALS AND OTHER GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL FOR FAILURE TO ACT ON COMPLAINTS OF, OR TO GIVE ASSISTANCE OR RENDER SERVICE TO MIGRANT WORKERS, THEIR FAMILIES AND OVERSEAS FILIPINOS IN DISTRESS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE `MIGRANT WORKERS AND OVERSEAS FILIPINOS ACT OF 1995'
rows.abstract: SEC. 24-A. PENALTIES. - WITHOUT PREJUDICE TO THE FILING OF CRIMINAL COMPLAINT, ANY PHILIPPINE CONSULATE OFFICIAL AND OTHER GOVERNMENT PERSONNEL WHO FAILS OR REFUSES TO RENDER THE SERVICES AND/OR ASSISTANCE PROVIDED IN TITLES III, IV AND V OF THIS ACT SHALL, AFTER DUE NOTICE AND HEARING, AND IF FOUND GUILTY, BE PUNISHED WITH SUSPENSION FROM OFFICE OF NOT LESS THAN THIRTY (30) DAYS OR DISMISSAL FROM THE SERVICE WITH FORFEITURE OF RETIREMENT AND OTHER BENEFITS, AND SHALL BE DISQUALIFIED FROM HOLDING ANY OTHER GOVERNMENT OFFICE.  FOR THIS PURPOSE, THE CENTER, IN COORDINATION WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT, SHALL FORMULATE THE NECESSARY RULES AND PROCEDURE FOR THE CONDUCT OF SUCH HEARING AND IMPOSITION OF APPROPRIATE PENALTIES.

rows.abstract: In addition to his duties and functions, the punong barangay is also tasked to: (16) ENFORCE ALL LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO THE PREVENTION, USE AND SALE OF ILLEGAL DRUGS. (17) PERFORM MINOR REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE OF MUNICIPAL AND BARANGAY ROADS IN COORDINATION WITH THE MAYORS OF THEIR RESPECTIVE MUNICIPALITIES OR CITIES. (18) CONDUCT ANNUALLY A CENSUS OF THE POPULATION OF BARANGAY AND SUBMIT THE RESULT OF SUCH CENSUS TO THE NATIONAL CENSUS STATISTICS OFFICE THROUGH THE MAYOR OF SUCH MUNICIPALITY OR CITY.

rows.abstract: The Secretary of National Defense and the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government may authorize lawyers of their respective departments to provide legal assistance and representation to any member of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Philippine National Police who is facing charges before fiscals and courts for any offense arising from or connected with the performance of his official duties. Should government lawyers be not readily available, lawyers from the private sectors may be hired to provide such legal assistance.

rows.abstract: Any person who has served in any branch of the government service either in the national government, Judiciary, Armed Forces of the Philippines, the Philippine National Police or government-owne d and/or controlled corporation shall be credited forthe length of service actually rendered upon reinstatement to another branch of service: Provided, That if the person has retired and subsequently reinstated in another branch or in the same branch of service, he shall be entitled to a retirement benefit equivalent to certain specified rates.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A PROGRAM OF EDUCATION DESIGNED TO HELP ALL MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY OF AN EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTION AVOID INVOLVEMENT WITH ILLEGAL DRUGS
rows.title_short: The Drug Abuse Prevention Program in Education Institution Act
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to institutionaliz e a community based program as a safeguard against the onslaught of drugs abuse that if unabated might become not only a serious social problem but even a threat to national security given the more contemporary backdrop.  In this regard, educational institutions shall establish drug counseling services and whenever possible, rehabilitation services as well as with members of the immediate community as beneficiaries.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-07-30, transmitted to on 2002-08-05 and received by the Senate on 2002-08-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW CIGARETTE AND/OR TOBACCO COMPANIES IN THE PHILIPPINES, PROHIBITING THE EXPANSION OF MANUFACTURING FACILITIES AND/OR PLANT CAPACITIES OF EXISTING CIGARETTE/TOBAC CO FIRMS AND CREATING A SPECIAL PRESIDENTIALCOMMISSION THAT WILL STUDY AND IMPLEMENT POLICIES AND PROCEDURES TOWARDS THE GRADUAL PHASE-OUT OF THE CIGARETTE AND TOBACCO INDUSTRY IN THE COUNTRY, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Cigarette and Tobacco Industry Control and Phase-out Act of 2001." Rationale: Time and again, cigarettes and tobacco products have been described as the last "legal drug." Any action, therefor, which tends to make these products available to a wider segment of the population - most especially the youth - should be discourage, if not rejected outright. That the Philippine government relies on tobacco investments is also a sign of desperation. lagging behind its Asian neighbors in terms of attracting much needed investments, the Philippines is hard-pressed to attract dollars to our shores, even if these dollars are blood money coming from the millions of people around the world who have died from smoking.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05950

rows.abstract: The position of Barangay Health Worker (BHW) is hereby created in every barangay in the Philippines. A BHW shall have the rank privileges of a barangay kagawad subject to adjustments approved by the Department of Budget and Management. > A BHW shallbe responsible for the year round implementation of the projects and programs of the Department of Health (DOH). Furthermore, BHWs shall initiate and plan such other programs as they may deem necessary for the advancement of health care program in their respective barangays and shall maintain close working relationship with the barangay captains, provincial/muni cipal health officers and non-government organizations.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to REDIRECT a portion of the charity fund of the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office to particular government institutions that can implement social welfare and health programs to the fullest. This proposed measure mandates that the Department of Health and Department of Social Welfare and Development receive fifteen (15%) and ten (10%) percent share, respectively, of the charing fund of the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office to finance its proprity programs, including thecontinuation of existing ones. This way, better coordination between agencies will be attained and continuity of long-term programs will be ensured.

rows.abstract: In 1973, President Ferdinand Marcos issued Presidential Decree 217, establishing the basic policies for the telephone industry. The decree aimed to attain an efficient telephone service for as wide an area as possible at the lowest reasonable cost to the subscriber.> The expansion of telephone service is not longer a problem, as there are authorized telephone service providers in all the regions of the country. It is on this premise that this bill is seeking to repeal PD 217.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF MICROBIOLOGY IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  At present, there are a number of universities that offer academic programs toward the production of graduates with training in microbiology. Those with training in microbiology have found jobs as quality control personnel in the manufacture of foods, pharmaceuticals , drugs, consmetics, food additives and flavors; as professional researcher in research institutes, biotechnology laboratories and in hospitals; as participant in the conduct of environmental impact studies; as instructor of microbiology courses in research institutes and centers, colleges and universities. Therefore, it becomes imperative that the practice of microbiology be regulated.
